A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Dreamweaver research. All 25 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-E, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original concept-discovery, video-generation, downstream reasoning, and ablation experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D, including quantitative results in Figure 3 and Table 2.

after.justification: v3 reports original DCI evaluations, compositional video generation, reasoning accuracy, and architectural ablations in Section 5 and Appendix D. These retained results qualify as original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: Sections 2-3 and Appendix B retain the same RBSU, prototype attention, block interaction, decoding procedures, and training objectives. The added statement about random prototype initialization documents an existing component without establishing a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Moving-Sprites, Moving-CLEVR, Moving-CLEVRTex, Dancing-Sprites, and Dancing-CLEVR. The compositional generation and reasoning tasks, withheld-combination evaluations, and unseen-shape/dynamics scenarios in Appendix D are unchanged.

E2.justification: RSSM, STEVE, and the recurrent adaptation of SysBinder remain the comparison methods in the corresponding DCI and downstream experiments (Figures 3, 5, and 12). The added Chen et al. citation is not an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, probing procedures, training settings in Table 1, and appendix protocols are unchanged. Both retain the 90%/10% combination split in Appendix D.2 and evaluation over 20 video scenarios in Table 2.

E4.justification: Section 5.4 retains the same architectural ablations and sensitivity analyses for blocks, concept memory, context length, and prediction length. Appendix D retains the same concept visualizations, manipulation examples, and OOD analyses.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the error bars in Figures 3 and 6. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The plotted results, qualitative examples, and numerical entries match. For example, Table 2 retains MSE values of 1261 for Moving-Sprites and 1484 for Dancing-CLEVR, with identical LPIPS and PSNR values.

T1.justification: The block-slot definitions, attention and recurrent equations, loss formulations, and Appendix B mathematics are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both retain the claims of unsupervised static and dynamic concept discovery, superior DCI performance, and compositional video generation. The revised title and wording about previously seen objects clarify the existing framing; the contribution paragraph and conclusion retain their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning predictive learning, concept memory, and generalization are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning uncertainty modeling, other abstract concepts, and complex scenes; Appendix A retains the limitation concerning object interactions.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly states that prototype vectors start with random values in Section 2.2 and adds a project-page URL to the abstract. Appendix C remains unchanged, and the reproducibility statement still promises a future code/data release; the PDFs do not establish that release.

R1.justification: v3 adds Chen et al. (2020), Generative pretraining from pixels, as a reference for the autoregressive image transformer in Section 3. The substantive related-work discussions in Section 4 and Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title changes from Learning Compositional World Representations from Pixels to Learning Compositional World Models from Pixels. Limited abstract, introduction, and method wording edits accompany revised acknowledgements and publication headers; the section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds ICLR publication headers, changes title wrapping and hyperlink/citation styling, and modestly reflows early pages and references. All 15 figures and seven tables retain their content, numbering, and display structures.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation and attribution through explicit random prototype initialization, a project-page pointer, and the added image-transformer reference. These provide limited clarity and discoverability benefits. The method, empirical evidence, and substantive limitations remain unchanged.
